review_of: CBSE PUA sanitizer after Codex PARTIAL audit

prior_audit.claim: Line-drop sanitizer removed mixed English/math lines on 248 of 256 changed questions

what_changed_since_partial: Current code no longer drops whole PUA lines. It strips E000-EFFF glyphs and keeps unique readable residue when English remains usable. Unreadable-only occurrences are left untouched so they stay review-flagged.

cited_examples_rechecked.e2x_ex_derivative: preserved after sanitizer; options ex / 2ex / 2e2x remain
cited_examples_rechecked.If A = 3B: preserved; sanitized text keeps If A = 3B and | B | = 2
cited_examples_rechecked.AA_prime_equals_9I: preserved; sanitized text keeps If A = ... AA' = 9I, find x

gaps_closed: Proved naive line-drop is harmful on this batch (217 unique-token losses).
Proved current sanitizer has 0 unique-token losses on the same 14 files.
Proved the three cited mixed-line examples now survive.
Did not edit sanitizer/parser/OCR files. Did not rebuild corpus.
residual_risks: 145 PUA questions are intentionally not sanitized because English residue is unusable; they should stay in review.
Staged text files still contain PUA; sanitizer runs only at corpus build time.
Final rebuild remains Codex-owned. This review does not claim the live question-syllabus sidecar already includes sanitized text.
recommendation_to_codex: Keep the residue-preserving sanitizer. Do not revert to whole-line PUA drops. Apply it on the single-owner final rebuild. No further sanitizer patch is required for the cited mixed-line failure mode.
